title: Least-privilege permission model for the coding harness
statement: Least-privilege permission model for the coding harness
body: Accepted. This includes the approval limits above as working values; the owner may change them under T13. - Adopt [permissions.json](../../harness/policy/permissions.json) as the policy-as-code source: tiers P0 to P4, environments, per-agent ceilings (P0 or P1 only, none for Azure), operations with tiers, classifiers, path classes, default rules DEF-01 to DEF-09 and extra rules CTL-01 and EXEC-01. - Enforce through [permission-engine.cjs](../../harness/hooks/permission-engine.cjs), called by the agent-scoped guard, the repository-wide guard and the output hook; deny unknown tools and operations for named agents; apply the always-on denials to every session. - P2 and above require a signed, expiring, scoped, use-limited approval naming exact agents and operations, verified with Ed25519 against a registry of public keys. The registry is empty, so every P2+ operation by an agent is denied until the owner registers approvers. P4 needs two distinct approvers and is never implied by a lower-tier approval. Some operations are never grantable to an agent. - Phase 0 permits no Azure or remote change whatever the approval. - Record every denial in a hash-chained, content-free audit log. - Specify, but do not create, Azure identities with a custom role excluding delete and authorization writes ([azure-identities.json](../../harness/policy/azure-identities.json)); specify GitHub protection with a read-only verifier and CODEOWNERS ([github-protection.json](../../harness/policy/github-protection.json)). Neither is applied. - Refuse shell commands built at run time as a never-grantable operation, classify direct ARM REST calls and Az PowerShell, and refuse egress in sessions scoped to isolated data. - Validate the model with `validate-permissions`, run negative tests in CI and treat [ENFORCEMENT-STATUS](../security/ENFORCEMENT-STATUS.md) as the authoritative list of what is enforced.
